newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close down, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close down, seen consolidating.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished down on Thursday, with investors taking profits against five straight sessions of gains, particularly in electronics, brokers said.
The weighted index climbed to an intra-day high of 8,317.79 before turning downward and sliding 51.61 points or 0.62 percent at 8,231.30 points at close.
Turnover was an active T$135.6 billion.
Brokers attributed the fall mainly to profit-taking on electronics, which had spearheaded the index's recent rebound.
The electronics sector declined 0.74 percent, with Taiwan Semiconductor down T$4 or 3.11 percent to T$124.5.
"Electronic shares were a bit too hot. It's necessary to have a break," said Yungli Securities analyst Chen Han-chung.
Computer giant Acer Inc fell T$2 or 2.4 percent to T$81.5 and semiconductor maker Winbond lost T$1 or 2.4 percent to T$40.6.

The market had opened higher on news that the central bank and watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission had agreed to speed up screening and approval procedures on foreign equity funds entering Taiwan's stock market.
"This move affirms the government's bullish towards the stock market," Chen said.
Textiles rose a scant 0.08 percent on minor bargain-hunting. Formosa Taffeta gained T$1.9 or 5.76 percent to T$34.9.
Brokers said the market would move around the 8,200-8,300 level until the trendsetting electronics shares finish their correction.
The late morning announcement of a small 0.75 percent annual rise in Taiwan's May consumer price index had no major impact, brokers said.
